newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary shares mixed, BUX hits 3rd successive high.
newsitem.headline: Hungary shares mixed, BUX hits 3rd successive high.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed mixed as the U.S. dollar failed to give a boost to the market, traders said.
"The dollar did not play too much of a role today," said Peter Tolgyesi of Buda-Cash Brokerhaz Kft.
The BUX index extended its recent gains to hit the third successive high of 3,835.95 points, rising 17.74 points.
Traders said the rise of the index was triggered mainly by the two chemicals stocks which hit new all-time highs.
TVK soared to a new record high of 1,725 forints before ending at 1,700, up 50.
Market participants said TVK shares have benefited from a recent "buy" recommendation by CS First Boston.
Borsodchem jumped to 3,895 forints before retreating to end at 3,870, up 20.
"Huge orders have been lodged for Borsodchem stocks in the past few days, mostly from U.S. funds, but also from U.K. funds," said Tibor Papp, salesman at Raiffeisen Securities, said earlier today.
"These orders may have stemmed from the company's roadshow a few months ago, which was linked to a private placement."
Good corporate news also backed Borsodchem's rise, he said, referring to recently published IAS results, expanded capacity and a good PVC price cycle in the last quarter of 1996.
Traders said some of the current share prices reflected expectations of the company's future performance.
"Price rises are in connections with expectations of the shares," Adam Santha of Daiwa-MKB Rt said.
He pointed to his expectations of TVK rising to above 2,000 forints soon. "Its daily turnover is very encouraging."
He said he was also referring to oil and gas company MOL which is expected to have a further tranche of privatisation sometimes next year.
MOL closed at 1,905 forints, below the day's peak of 1,910, but above Friday's close orf 1,895.
